(Gondal), in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.116 of 2006, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.74,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant, holding the opponents i.e. owner, driver and insurance company liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
On 09.07.2005, the applicant was traveling in the vehicle Tata 709, No.
GJ-120-8657, along with a Pig (Animal), going from Jamnagar to Ahmedabad.

When he reached National Highway No. 8-A near Bamanbor Bypass at about 01:30 a.m.,
the driver of Tata 709, No. GJ-12-U-8657, drove his vehicle with full speed, recklessly and negligently, endangering human life, without observing traffic rules and dashed with the truck ahead of the vehicle on which the applicant was traveling.
Thus, this accident occurred.
Due to this accident, the applicant sustained serious fracture injuries on his left leg and other grievous bodily injuries, resulting in permanent disability.
Hence, the claim petition has been filed by the claimant to get the compensation of Rs.5 lakhs with 18% per annum interest.
2.2. Notices were served to the opponents.
None were present except Opponents No.3 - insurance company.

Opponent No.3 - insurance company has filed its written statement at Exh.23 by disputing all the averments NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3. The Tribunal has framed the issues at Exh.29.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the various documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal has been preferred by claimant - before this Court for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.

4.1. Learned advocate Mr. Tushar L. Sheth for the appellant - original claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has erred in not granting any amount on the head of future loss of income merely on the ground that the injured claimant died after 11 years of filling the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined claim petition and it is admitted by the father of the deceased that his son died due to natural death.

Furthermore, he has submitted that the Tribunal has failed to appreciate that the injured claimant had received serious fracture injuries on his left leg and also received other injuries on his entire body, the injured was sifted to Civil Hospital, Rajkot where he was treated from 9.7.2005 to 14.7.2005 as indoor patient, he was operated there and screw and plate were fixed in his leg, thereafter also, due to complications, the injured was shifted to Ratnam Hospital, Rajkot, and he was again operated there, he was bedridden for about 6 months and his treatment continued.
The injured was suffering from 38% permanent disability as per the disability certificate issued by Dr. Langaliya.

4.2. Furthermore, he has submitted that the Tribunal has failed to appreciate that at the time of accident, the injured was doing labour work and was earning Rs.200/- per day and due to accident, he was not in a position to do the same work due to serious injuries sustained by him.
Considering the disability certificate, the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined injured at least Rs.3,500/- per month.

He has submitted that at the Mansukhbhai Naranbhai Patoliya vs Lalo Alias Sureshbhai Jadavbhai Parmar on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142359462/
2 time of accident, the injured was aged about 30 years, the accident took place on 9.7.2005 and injured passed away on 24.7.2016, therefore, multiplier of 11 is required to be applied in the present case while calculating future prospective income of the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Furthermore, he has submitted that the Tribunal ought to have appreciated that the injured was aged about 30 years and, therefore,
the Tribunal ought to have added 100% rise in income.
4.3. Furthermore, he has submitted that Tribunal ought to have granted Rs.1,25,000/- for medical expenses.
The Ld. Judge ought to have awarded Rs.1,00,000/- pain, shock and suffering.

The Ld.
Judge ought to have awarded Rs.1,00,000/- for transportation, special diet, attendant charges.
The Ld. Judge ought to have awarded Rs.21,000/- for actual loss of income as injured was bedridden for a period of 6 month.
Hence, he has submitted that in view of the above referred premises, the quantum of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal is on a lower side against the well-establish principles of law.
Therefore, he has prayed to allow the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined present appeal by enhancing the amount of compensation.

5. Per contra, learned advocate Mr. Makbul I. Mansuri for the defendant No.2 and learned advocate Mr. Yogi K. Gadhia for the defendant No. 3 have jointly submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, as the Tribunal has considered all the aspects and passed the impugned judgment and award after considering the material available on the record.

However, from the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellant that the Tribunal has committed certain errors, on this aspect, learned advocates for the respondents have submitted that if this Court feels that there is some error in calculation of the amount in view of settled position of law, in awarding compensation by the Tribunal, then the Court may pass appropriate order by considering the submissions made by him, in the interest of justice.
Accordingly, both the learned advocates have jointly submitted the calculation fort the agreed amount.
5.1. I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.

I have gone through the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED:
11/06/2024 undefined judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
5.2. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness,
reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
5.3. It is evident from the record that the accident occurred on 09.07.2005, and the claim petition was filed in the year 2006.
It is the case of the claimant that they sustained serious bodily injuries and permanent disablement due to the accident.
After the accident, the appellant - claimant was shifted to the Government Hospital, Rajkot, and remained an indoor patient for a long time.

Hence, the claimant - injured has filed claim petition for getting the compensation of Rs.5 lakh with NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED:
11/06/2024 undefined interest.

In response, the Tribunal, via judgment and award dated 28.08.2018, has awarded the amount of Rs.74,000/- with 9% p.a. interest, holding opponent Nos. 1 to 3, i.e., the owner, driver, and insurance company, respectively liable, jointly and severally liable.

5.4. I have considered the written statement filed by opponent No. 3 - the insurance company at Mansukhbhai Naranbhai Patoliya vs Lalo Alias Sureshbhai Jadavbhai Parmar on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142359462/
3 Exh.23, the deposition of the witness - father of the deceased below Exh.35, the injury certificate, as well as the disability certificate, which are produced in support of the claimant's case.

sentences.text: It also transpires from other medical papers that the Tribunal has awarded the amount of Rs.74,000/- for compensation, which is, prima facie, found to be on the lower side.
Therefore, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the same, the claimant has preferred the present appeal for enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

5.5. Furthermore, the Tribunal has erred in not considering the income of the claimant - the injured properly, who died after a period of eleven years from the accident, and died a natural death, as deposed by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined the father of the deceased.

At the time of the accident, the claimant - injured was working in diamond polishing and animal catching, and the Tribunal has considered income of the claimant - injured,
Rs.2,000/-.
Considering the minimum wages prevailing in the year 2005, the income of the claimant - injured party should be considered Rs.2,500/- instead of Rs.2,000/- as considered by the Tribunal.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the income of the claimant - injured should be considered Rs.2,500/- per month.
Therefore, annual income of claimant - injured comes to Rs.30,000/-. 5.6.
Furthermore, the disability certificate is on record.

Considering the fact that both the appellant and respondent have agreed to consider disability to the extent of 17%, even though the certificate indicates a higher percentage of disability, I am of the opinion that the disability of the claimant - injured should be considered to the extent of 17%.
5.7. As agreed by both the learned advocates, the multiplier of 11 is considered, considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case.
5.8. Furthermore, the Tribunal has not awarded any NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined amount towards future loss of income.

In view of the fact that this Court has considered the claimant's monthly income Rs. 2,500/-, instead of Rs. 2,000/-, resulting in an annual income of Rs.
30,000/-, and considering the disability to the extent of 17% and the multiplier of 11 as agreed by the parties, which are required to be considered in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
Hence, the amount towards loss of future income comes to Rs. 56,100/-.
The actual loss considered by the Tribunal is Rs.4,000/- for two months, based on a monthly income of Rs. 2,000/-.
As this Court has considered the monthly income of the claimant - injured as Rs. 2,500/-, the actual loss of income amounts to Rs.5,000/-, instead of Rs. 4,000/-.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-
towards medical expenses, which is in accordance with the medical bills and thus, deemed just and proper, requiring no interference.

Similarly, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards transportation, which is also found just and proper given the facts and circumstances of the case,
requiring no interference.

Additionally, the Tribunal has awarded Rs. 50,000/- towards pain, shock,
and suffering, which is considered just and proper, taking into account the period of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined hospitalization and the nature of the claimant's injuries, and thus requires no interference.

5.9. Thus, the appellant - claimant is entitled to get the following final amount as compensation:

only under various heads.
The appellant - original claimant is entitled to get the additional amount of compensation of Rs.57,100/- over and above the amount of Rs.74,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.

The opponents, including the insurance company, are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid additional amount of Rs.57,100/- to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/232/2020 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined appellant - original claimant together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.
Rest of the direction(s) if any, shall remain same.
6. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
6.1. The present appeal is partly allowed.

6.2. The impugned judgment and award dated 28.08.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.) (Gondal), in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.116 of 2006 shall stand modified to the aforesaid extent by enhancing the amount of compensation as above.
